body:
Terrain-only fertility already stays cached during ordinary gameplay, but any terrain-ID change discarded the fields, and an edit-batch commit could discard a cache rebuilt after its last edit. Compare actual ecology inputs instead: habitat-only changes update one resource mask, unrelated capability changes retain the fields, and map replacement or changed donor/inhibition/shore/growth inputs invalidate them.

Reorganize the exact land and aquatic kernels into padded rows/diagonals and contiguous destination spans. The formulas, integer rounding, RNG, save/replay formats and intended gameplay feel are unchanged. Existing direct-oracle tests now retain thin and rectangular map coverage.

Measured land + aquatic rebuild medians on three generated maps improve 27–49%: the 512² river map falls from 78.85 to 40.31 ms. The dense 512² synthetic fixture falls from 353.89 to 165.24 ms. No steady-state FPS gain is claimed: final GDB measurement observes one rebuild over 512 growth ticks. Persistent memory is unchanged; aquatic peak temporary allocation increases 238 KiB at 512², while land peak allocation decreases.

Verification:795 headless unit cases and267 focused engine cases pass, including warmed-cache save/load, tiling/import, AI farming, JavaScript and match-record goldens. Three maps each match 4096 per-tick checksums against the retained previous engine and across current serial/parallel execution. Independent review checked 272 direct oracle cases under native ASan/UBSan and ARM64 QEMU. A pointer-padding finding was fixed and independently retested.

Full-engine non-Linux platform runs and visual tests were not performed; ARM64 coverage is kernel-only. Detailed commands, provenance, measurements and remotely accessible evidence are in the verification comment. No simulation revision bump because outputs remain identical.
